title: Access to Part D Vaccines
canonicalText:
[[MA.6112 | Access to Part D Vaccines | Applies to: OneCare | Revised 12/01/2024]]
<<page 1>>
I. PURPOSE
This policy defines the process for the provision of covered Part D Vaccines dispensed and administered
to CalOptima Health Members.
II. POLICY
A. CalOptima Health shall ensure that a Member has adequate access to covered Part D Vaccines
  dispensed and administered in a Physician’s office.
B. A covered Part D Vaccine shall include vaccines not available for reimbursement under Medicare
  Parts A or B and when administration is reasonable and necessary for the prevention of illness.
C. The following vaccines shall be excluded from Part D and covered under Medicare Part B:
  1. Pneumococcal pneumonia vaccine;
  2. Hepatitis B vaccine for individuals at high or intermediate risk;
    a. High risk groups currently identified include:
      i. Individuals with End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD);
      ii. Individuals with diabetes;
      iii. Individuals with hemophilia who received Factor VIII or IX concentrates;
      iv. Clients of institutions for the mentally handicapped;
      v. Persons who live in the same household as a hepatitis B Virus (HBV) carrier;
      vi. Homosexual men; and
      vii. Illicit injectable drug abusers.
    b. Intermediate risk groups include:
<<page 2>>
      i. Staff in institutions for the mentally handicapped; and
      ii. Workers in health care professions who have frequent contact with blood or blood-
        derived body fluids during routine work.
  3. COVID-19
  4. Influenza virus vaccine; and
  5. Other vaccines (e.g., tetanus toxoid) when directly related to the treatment of an injury or direct
    exposure to a disease or condition.
D. A CalOptima Health Network Pharmacy may provide covered Part D Vaccines directly to a
  Physician office.
E. A CalOptima Health Member may receive covered Part D Vaccines directly from a Physician
  office.
F. A CalOptima Health Member may receive covered Part D Vaccines directly from a Network
  Pharmacy.
G. Reimbursement for covered Part D Vaccines shall include vaccine administration costs, dispensing
  fee (if applicable), and vaccine ingredient cost.
H. Members shall be responsible for the co-payment associated with the covered Part D Vaccine.
III. PROCEDURE
A. In-Network Pharmacy Distribution of Covered Part D Vaccines
  1. A Member may obtain a prescription from a prescribing Provider and bring it to a CalOptima
    Health pharmacy for administration.
  2. A Member may obtain a covered Part D Vaccine from a Network Pharmacy and bring it to a
    Physician or other prescribing Provider for administration.
  3. A CalOptima Health pharmacy may ship the prescribed drug or vaccine directly to the
    Physician and bill CalOptima Health for the covered Part D Vaccine; CalOptima Health will not
    be responsible for the cost of shipping.
B. Prescriber and Out-of-Network Pharmacy Distribution of Covered Part D Vaccines
  1. A Physician or other prescribing Provider may administer a covered Part D Vaccine and bill
    CalOptima Health on a CMS-1500 form.
  2. CalOptima Health Pharmacy Department will review the submitted form and Member
    pharmacy claims history:
    a. To apply utilization management edits, such as ensuring the absence of duplicate claims for
      the same vaccine; and
<<page 3>>
    b. To ensure its administration is consistent with Advisory Committee on Immunization
      Practices (ACIP) recommendations.
  3. CalOptima Health Pharmacy Department will coordinate with the Claims Department to
    provide payment to the Provider for the ingredient cost of the vaccine, plus administration fee.
  4. CalOptima Health may authorize Member reimbursement for payment of covered Part D
    Vaccines:
    a. If a Member pays for a covered Part D Vaccine in the Physician’s office, the Member shall
      contact the CalOptima Health Customer Service Department and provide record of
      payment.
    b. The CalOptima Health Customer Service Department shall coordinate an evaluation of a
      Member’s reimbursement request with the Pharmacy Management Department.
    c. CalOptima Health shall refund a Member for the approved medications and administration
      of the vaccine less any applicable cost sharing, consistent with CalOptima Health Policy
      MA.6101: Medicare Part D Coverage Determination.
C. Covered Part D Vaccine claims shall be processed by the Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) for
  inclusion in Prescription Drug Event (PDE) records.
V. REFERENCE(S)
A. CalOptima Health Contract with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) for
  Medicare Advantage
B. CalOptima Health Policy MA.6101: Medicare Part D Coverage Determination
C. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Part D Application 2015
D. “Increasing Part D Vaccine Access,” Health Plan Management System (HPMS) Memorandum,
  Issued 05/08/2006
E. Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, Chapter 6: Revised 01/15/2016
F. MLN Matters® Number: SE0727 Revised 01/14/2013
G. “Part D Vaccines,” Health Plan Management System (HPMS) Memorandum, Issued 12/01/2006
H. Medicare.gov Your Medicare Coverage Hepatitis B Shots; Accessed 07/18/2022
<<page 5>>
IX. GLOSSARY
End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD): That stage of kidney impairment that appears irreversible and permanent and requires a regular course of dialysis or kidney transplantation to maintain life. End Stage Renal Disease is classified as Stage V of Chronic Kidney Disease. This stage exists when renal function, as measured by glomerular filtration rate (GFR), is less than 15ml/min/1.73m2 and serum creatinine is greater than or equal to eight, unless the Member is diabetic, in which case serum creatinine is greater than or equal to six (6). Excretory, regulatory, and hormonal renal functions are severely impaired, and the Member cannot maintain homeostasis.
Medicare Part B Vaccines: Medicare Part B covered vaccines include Hepatitis B, Influenza virus, Pneumococcal, and other vaccines directly related to the treatment of an injury or direct exposure to a disease or condition.
Medicare Part D Vaccines: Medicare Part D vaccines are those not covered by Part B and used as reasonable and necessary to prevent illness.
Member: A beneficiary enrolled in a CalOptima Health program.
Network Pharmacy: For the purposes of this policy, refers to a licensed pharmacy that is under contract to provide covered Part D drugs and other pharmacy services CalOptima Health Members.
Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM): An entity that provides pharmacy benefit management services, including contracting with a network of pharmacies; establishing payment levels for network pharmacies; negotiating rebate arrangements; developing and managing formularies, preferred drug lists, and prior authorization programs; maintaining patient compliance programs; performing drug utilization review; and operating disease management programs.
Primary Care Practitioner/Physician (PCP): A Practitioner/Physician responsible for supervising, coordinating, and providing initial and primary care to Members and serves as the medical home for Members. The PCP is a general practitioner, internist, pediatrician, family practitioner, or obstetrician/gynecologist (OB/GYN). For Members who are Seniors or Persons with Disabilities or eligible for the Whole Child Model, “Primary Care Practitioner” or “PCP” shall additionally mean any Specialty Care Provider who is a Participating Provider and is willing to perform the role of the PCP. A PCP may also be a Non-Physician Medical Practitioner (NMP) (e.g., Nurse Practitioner [NP], Nurse Midwife, Physician Assistant [PA]) authorized to provide primary care services under supervision of a Physician. For SPD or Whole Child Model beneficiaries, a PCP may also be a Specialty Care Provider or clinic.
Provider (Part D): All contracted Providers including physicians, Non-physician Medical Practitioners, ancillary providers, and facilities or institutions who are licensed to furnish Covered Services.
